citation: LinearB, '2026 Software Engineering Benchmarks Report: The AI productivity edition', 48-page PDF, created 9 Dec 2025. https://assets.linearb.io/image/upload/v1765300694/resources/LinearB_2026_Software_Engineering_Benchmarks_Report.pdf (landing page https://linearb.io/resources/engineering-benchmarks-report)
source_tier: Vendor research (LinearB sells software engineering intelligence / AI productivity tooling)
access_status: Fully read via local text extraction (pdftotext) of the downloaded PDF. Relevant pages (PR size p.17-18, pickup/review p.19-20, acceptance p.12-13 and p.21-23, conclusion p.38) read in full. Other-site secondary coverage seen only as search snippets and not relied on.
sponsor_and_incentive: Produced by LinearB itself. It sells engineering metrics and AI-productivity tooling, and frames AI productivity as 'the next evolution of Software Engineering Intelligence'. Findings showing AI friction in review support its product category. The survey part also has the vendor's selection of respondents.
exact_quotes: "CREATED FROM A STUDY OF 8.1+ M PRS FROM 4,800 ENGINEERING TEAMS ACROSS 42 COUNTRIES." (cover, p.1)
"At the p75 mark, Agentic AI PRs reach 293 lines of code compared to 157 lines for Unassisted PRs, which means reviewers suddenly have much more to process." (p.17)
"AI-Assisted PRs are now the largest of all three groups, hitting 408 lines at P75" (p.18)
"[INSIGHT 02] Agentic AI PRs have a PR Pickup Time 5.3x longer than Unassisted ones." (p.19)
"At the P75 mark, Agentic AI PRs sit idle for 1,055 minutes before a reviewer even opens them, compared to just 201 minutes for Unassisted PRs." (p.20)
"With manual PRs merging at 84.4% and AI PRs merging at just 32.7%, teams are clearly treating AI-generated code differently." (p.21)
"Some of this gap likely stems from unclear ownership: the AI PRs don't typically have a natural human owner whose goal is to get them approved and merged." (p.21)
"context (not just correctness) is the single biggest barrier to merging AI-generated PRs." (p.13, survey commentary)
"Acceptance Rate is the percentage of PRs that get merged within X=30 days of being created (or moved out of draft)." (p.12)
"Heavier Agentic AI adoption is not translating to greater value delivery." / "orgs with higher AI PR adoption rarely outperform those with lower adoption." (p.22-23)
"Leaders described AI-driven reviews as faster yet more shallow" and "A larger amount of code slips into production without proper review (rubber stamping)." (p.20)
"For aggregation, we used the P75 (75th percentile) calculation." (p.3)
key_claims: AI involvement makes PRs bigger, slower to be picked up and far less likely to merge. Agentic AI PRs (Devin, Copilot Coding Agent, Codex style) wait about 5.3x longer for a first reviewer than unassisted PRs, then get reviewed relatively quickly or shallowly. Agentic AI PRs merge within 30 days far less often than manual PRs. Higher AI adoption does not lift acceptance, except for one outlier org using Devin. The report attributes this to missing context, unclear ownership (no human champion), low-priority work given to agents, and reviewer distrust of larger diffs. It does not show that context packets or small PRs raise first-pass acceptance as a measured result; it only reports leaders saying missing context is the main barrier and, separately, that only about 22% strongly agree their team works in small batches (readiness survey).
headline_figures: PR size, P75 lines (p.17): Agentic AI 293, AI-Assisted 408, Unassisted 157. Median lines: Agentic 89, AI-Assisted 96, Unassisted 26. LEAD CHECK: '157' is the P75 for unassisted, NOT an average. 'Over 400' matches AI-assisted P75 (408), not an average and not agentic (293). Median gap is larger (about 3.4x to 3.7x). Report headline 'AI-Assisted PRs are 2.6x larger than Unassisted' equals 408/157 at P75. The '2.5x larger' lead is close to but not the report's 2.6x (AI-assisted) and agentic is 1.9x at P75 (293/157) and 3.4x at median (89/26).

Pickup time, P75, minutes (p.19-20): Agentic 1,055; AI-Assisted 496; Unassisted 201. Agentic/Unassisted = 5.25, reported as 5.3x. AI-Assisted/Unassisted = 2.5x (computed by me, not stated). LEAD CHECK: '5x longer' matches agentic only, P75, in minutes (about 17.6 h vs 3.4 h), not all AI PRs. The ~5x 'AI PRs 2.5x larger and waiting 5x longer' pairing mixes groups: the 2.5x pickup applies to AI-assisted, 5.3x to agentic.
Review time after pickup, P75, minutes (p.20): Agentic 382; AI-Assisted 194; Unassisted 252. AI-assisted PRs are reviewed faster than unassisted.

Acceptance rate, 30-day merge (p.21): Manual/non-AI 84.4%; AI PRs 32.7%. The report text says 'less than half'. The chart label says 'AI PRs'; benchmark table (p.12) is for Agentic AI PRs, so the 32.7% group is probably agentic [uncertain]. Not split out for AI-assisted.

Acceptance benchmark tiers (p.12): Manual PRs elite >95%, good 92-95%, fair 87-91%, needs focus <87%. Agentic AI PRs elite >71%, good 61-71%, fair 42-60%, needs focus <42%. 'Most teams find it hard to exceed 60%' for AI PRs.
Commit-level (p.18): assisted commits average 4.2 files vs 7.51 unassisted; 273 vs 498 lines per commit; 65 vs 66 lines per file. So AI commits are smaller but PRs larger.
Context packets: no figure. Not found. Small PRs: no figure linking PR size to acceptance in the AI section. Lead not supported by the report.
sample_and_method: About 8.1 million PRs from 4,800 engineering teams in 42 countries, observed delivery data (anonymised and normalised), aggregated at P75 for the published benchmarks. Three PR types: Agentic AI (agent opens the PR, e.g. Devin, Copilot Coding Agent, Codex), AI-Assisted (authored or significantly shaped with AI tools, human integrates), Unassisted. The report does not say how many PRs fall in each group or how AI involvement was detected [uncertain]. Time window of PR data not stated in the pages read [uncertain]. A separate AI in Engineering Leadership Survey (engineering executives, platform and DevEx leaders; November 2025 usage question) supplies self-reported quotes; respondent count not found in the text read [uncertain].
limitations: Stated: MTTR dropped because definitions vary too much; P75 used to limit outlier effect. Not stated but visible: vendor-authored; no sample counts per PR type; no confounder control (agentic PRs often target low-priority backlog work, which the report itself concedes); acceptance is merge within 30 days, so abandonment and low priority count as rejection, not poor quality; P75 not mean, so 'average' phrasing is wrong; survey is qualitative and self-selected; correlation only, no causal test that context or smaller PRs fix anything; pickup time measured in minutes at P75 and the 5.3x depends on the unassisted P75 of 201 minutes.
what_a_leader_can_do: The report supports naming a human owner for every AI PR, routing agent work to someone accountable, and giving reviewers intent and context. It also supports watching pickup time and acceptance as separate AI metrics and expecting tool-by-tool differences (acceptance varies widely by tool; one Devin-heavy org near parity). Evidence strength is weak to moderate: observational vendor data plus leader opinion, with the ownership explanation hedged ('likely stems from'). Evidence that small PRs or context packets lift first-pass acceptance is NOT in this report.
overlap_with_site_essays: Strong overlap with Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part and What It Takes to Trust Agent Output (missing context, trust, reviewer hesitation, shallow review, rubber stamping). Some overlap with The Verification Gap and Checking Isn't Catching: fast, shallow reviews once started and 'slips into production without proper review' are survey quotes, not measured defect data.
uncertain: sample_and_method: per-group PR counts, detection method, time window and survey n not found
headline_figures: whether the 32.7% acceptance figure refers to agentic PRs only or all AI PRs
